item.title: Java Programming Study Guide - AiiTE Q Dump-Set_8_Update
item.description:
Beginner

  1. Write a Palindrome program?

Intermediate

  1. Input: int [] = [1,0,0,2,0,0,0,3], Output: [1,2,3,0,0,0]. (Moving non-zero elements to the front)?

Questions with Answers

Beginner

1. Write a Palindrome program?

Solution:

String s = "madam";
String rev = new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString();
boolean isPal = s.equals(rev);

Intermediate

1. Input: int [] = [1,0,0,2,0,0,0,3], Output: [1,2,3,0,0,0]. (Moving non-zero elements to the front)?

Solution:

int[] arr = {1, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 3};
int[] res = new int[arr.length];
int j = 0;
for(int x : arr) if(x != 0) res[j++] = x;
// res will be [1, 2, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]

item.title: Java Programming Study Guide - OOPS
item.description:
Intermediate

  1. Demonstrate Upcasting in a main method?
  2. Demonstrate the use of abstract class and private fields with getters?

Advanced

  1. Write a program that demonstrates the four pillars of OOPS (Abstraction, Encapsulation, Inheritance, and Polymorphism) using an Animal superclass and a Dog subclass?

Questions with Answers

Intermediate

1. Demonstrate Upcasting in a main method?

Solution:

class Parent { void show() { System.out.println("Parent"); } }
class Child extends Parent { void show() { System.out.println("Child"); } }

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Parent obj = new Child(); // Upcasting
        obj.show(); // Calls Child's method (Runtime Polymorphism)
    }
}
